main.formula: no WebGPU on this page (0016 §1's 110 B floor does not apply): measured harness overhead, ceil(max of 50 clean runs = 45.43-45.55 B/frame) = 46, + 8 B margin (0016 §1's own margin convention) = 54 Fix round 3 (same Deviations): re-measured after the warm-up was split into 8 passes -- a constant 43.47 B/frame across 8 clean runs, under the unchanged 54.

sim.formula: 0016 §1: the strict worker figure. Re-measured post fix-round-2 (docs/plan/06b-workers-and-spawn.md, Deviations): `EngineInstance.call0`'s own detach check (`packages/engine/src/loader.ts`) now reads `ArrayBuffer.prototype.detached` instead of `TypedArray.prototype.byteLength === 0` (the old comparison boxed a fresh HeapNumber on an unpredictable fraction of calls, the source of `gc: flat transport parity`'s run-to-run mismatches on this isolate); the new accessor costs a slightly higher but now perfectly reproducible constant, 3.85 B/frame (2308 B / 600) every run, comfortably under 8 and not higher than this code already measured before this fix (2252-2444 B observed pre-fix on the same commit, the '1784' this formula previously cited having gone stale before this session) Fix round 3 (same Deviations): the "perfectly reproducible" claim above was wrong -- 2308 B was the low reading and 2448 B (+136 B, one feedback-vector allocation for the harness worker's own `armedLoop`) the high one, which is what `gc: flat transport parity` kept catching. With the warm-up split into 8 passes so that path is warm before the window, this isolate measures a constant 3.62 B/frame (2172 B / 600) across 8 clean runs and under both CDP transports.

main.formula: 0016 §1 margin convention. Fix round 2, second pass (docs/plan/06b-workers-and-spawn.md, Deviations): the prior 52-budget round masked two real per-pass allocation bugs in the production blocking loop (worker/shell.ts's NO_TIMEOUT re-boxing Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY every pass; worker/client.ts's frame(t_ms) call boxing a Float64Array read every real frame) behind STEP_TICK_EVERY=2 and 'sibling-burst headroom'. With both fixed and STEP_TICK_EVERY removed (ticks every frame again): clean max of 8 runs = 41.65 B/frame, ceil = 42, + 8 B margin = 50, no sibling headroom needed -- a sibling isolate's own `burst` control now measures main at 43.5-43.8 (was 44+ before), comfortably under 50. `object` control on `main` itself measured 66.7, `burst` on `main` itself ~40071, both far above. Fix round 3 (same Deviations): re-measured after the warm-up split and the yield-protocol lost-wake fix -- clean max of 8 runs = 39.73 B/frame, under the unchanged 50.

client.formula: 0016 §1: the strict worker figure. Fix round 2, second pass: the prior 33-budget accommodated frame(t_ms)'s own Float64Array-read box (12 B/frame) plus a sibling-burst swing; with worker/client.ts passing a constant instead (Deviations, 'frame(t_ms)') and worker/shell.ts's NO_TIMEOUT fixed, clean max of 8 runs = 1.19 B/frame and a sibling's own `burst` control no longer raises it (1.19-1.31 seen either way). `object` control on `client` itself measured 24.28-24.56, `burst` ~40058, both well above 8. Fix round 3 (same Deviations): now a constant 2.52 B/frame over 8 clean runs (up from 1.19 because the split warm-up moves which one-off allocations fall inside the window, down from unstable), still far under 8.
